status: Research designs only; these candidates are not registered benchmark scenarios.
priority_meaning: P1 is a proposed first implementation/evaluation wave; P2 is a follow-up or contract-validation wave. Priority is a hypothesis, not measured skill efficacy or production frequency.

common_evaluation.prompt_policy: Identical natural task prompts; no mention of skills or instruction to seek a particular source.
common_evaluation.knowledge_fairness: All decisive facts must be available through ordinary state inspection and the same public documentation accessible to both arms.
common_evaluation.success_policy: Independent functional and scope-preservation oracle; a skill read is not required for task success.
measurements: correct repair or supported blocked outcome
common_evaluation.holdouts: Separate development cases used to write the skill from held-out fault variants, names, versions and resource values.
common_evaluation.promotion_gate: Prescreen the no-skills agent. Prefer cases with repeatable searches, wrong branches, or avoidable operations; do not claim a content benefit when skills were unread. Freeze sources, feature versions and catalogs before paired trials.

candidates.task: Adopt an existing namespace into ARM management without changing live configuration.
candidates.prompt: Bring the existing {namespace} namespace under AKS managed-namespace control. Preserve its workloads, quota, network policies, labels and annotations; do not recreate it or force an overwrite. Verify management and workload continuity.
candidates.decision_boundary: IfIdentical requires the proposed managed fields to match existing state; Always can overwrite them, while Never rejects an existing namespace.
skill_outline: Read the target namespace and managed fields once.
Construct the ARM definition from observed state, not default quota/policy guesses.
Use IfIdentical for preservation; diagnose a mismatch instead of changing to Always.
Verify namespace/workload UIDs and managed configuration.
fixture_state: existing Kubernetes namespace UID and children
negative_controls: accepting a failed IfIdentical operation as success

value_hypothesis.searches: One procedure replaces separate adoption-policy, quota and lifecycle lookups.
value_hypothesis.actions: Avoid failed adoption loops and accidental overwrite attempts.

candidates.version_notes: Pin managedNamespaces API/CLI support and exact reconciliation rules; normalize equivalent CPU/memory quantities before comparing state.

candidates.task: Remove ARM management while keeping the namespace and its workloads.
candidates.prompt: Stop managing {namespace} through ARM while keeping the Kubernetes namespace, applications and stored data intact. Verify that only the management resource is removed.
candidates.decision_boundary: Keep deletes the ARM management resource but retains the namespace; Delete removes the namespace and its contents.
skill_outline: Capture delete policy and resource identities.
Set Keep if needed, then delete only the ARM resource.
Verify ARM absence and retained Kubernetes namespace, workload readiness and data identity.
negative_controls: recreate resources with the same names

value_hypothesis.searches: Resolve an unfamiliar lifecycle option without scanning the full managed-namespace guide.
value_hypothesis.actions: Avoid the destructive Kubernetes delete path and skip an unnecessary policy update when Keep is already set.

candidates.version_notes: Validate cleanup of managed child quota/policy resources before asserting their exact post-delete state; the primary contract is namespace/workload/data retention.

candidates.task: Repair namespace access when ARM visibility works but Kubernetes reads are forbidden.
candidates.prompt: The developer can see {namespace} in Azure and retrieve its connection settings, but cannot list its pods. Grant only the approved read access in this namespace and verify that secrets and other namespaces remain inaccessible.
candidates.decision_boundary: Namespace User/Contributor are management-plane roles; Kubernetes data-plane Reader/Writer/Admin have different permissions and scopes.
skill_outline: Confirm authentication and the exact forbidden operation.
Inspect the intended principal's management and data-plane roles separately.
Grant the approved namespace-scoped data-plane role and verify positive and negative access probes.

discovery.gap: Role-assignment and kubectl help are outside the current AKS-only overlay.

success_oracle: no admin credentials or cluster-wide grant

value_hypothesis.searches: Condense two role taxonomies and their scopes.
value_hypothesis.actions: Avoid repeated credential downloads and broad privilege grants.

candidates.version_notes: Pin the managed-namespace resource scope and API version; do not assume classic namespace scopes and managedNamespaces IDs are interchangeable.

candidates.task: Allow a designated cross-namespace ingress source while preserving isolation.
candidates.prompt: Restore traffic from the approved ingress-controller namespace to {service}. Keep unrelated namespaces denied and retain the existing namespace management and egress behavior. Verify both allowed and denied paths.
candidates.decision_boundary: Standard NetworkPolicy permissions combine additively; an allow-all policy is not narrowed by adding another restrictive-looking policy.
skill_outline: Inspect generated policy kinds and all selectors applying to the destination.
Reason about effective allowed traffic, not policy names or evaluation order.
Apply only the approved selective rule through the appropriate owner interface.
Verify ingress succeeds from the approved source and fails from unrelated sources.

discovery.gap: A kubectl-only diagnosis may never expose the AKS skill entry.

negative_controls: edit an ARM-owned policy through kubectl

value_hypothesis.searches: Resolve managed-policy ownership and additive semantics together.
value_hypothesis.actions: Avoid changes that appear restrictive but broaden effective access.

candidates.version_notes: Validation gate: inspect generated resource kinds before choosing the correct repair. The managed-namespace guide's AllowAll-then-restrict wording must not override standard NetworkPolicy union semantics.

candidates.task: Restore pulls after a registry changes to ABAC repository permissions.
candidates.prompt: Restore the deployment's pulls of {image} from the existing registry. Preserve private access and the image reference. Grant only the kubelet's approved repository pull access, without push or administrative permissions, and verify a new pod pulls the image.
candidates.decision_boundary: ABAC mode does not honor classic AcrPull; Repository Reader and an approved condition may be required. The pull identity is the kubelet identity.
skill_outline: Classify the full pull error before assigning roles.
Read registry permission mode and the actual kubelet principal.
Repair the approved role/condition once and allow propagation.
Verify the intended image pull, not the caller's registry listing.

discovery.gap: ACR/role help is outside the current overlay.

success_oracle: fresh pull of intended image succeeds as kubelet
other repositories and push remain denied
negative_controls: unconditioned registry-wide Reader when only one repository is approved
add Catalog Lister solely to prove pull access
held_out_variants: correct role but wrong repository condition

value_hypothesis.searches: Avoid separate identity, ABAC-role and attach-acr limitation lookups.
value_hypothesis.actions: Avoid ineffective role assignments and privilege expansion.

candidates.version_notes: Pin registry role-assignment mode and evaluate effective repository access; role creation alone is not success.

candidates.task: Repair layer download failures when registry login and manifest access work.
candidates.prompt: Image pulls authenticate and resolve the manifest but fail while downloading layers. Restore pulls while keeping the registry private and retaining current permissions and image references.
candidates.decision_boundary: Login and data endpoints are different; successful authentication does not establish blob/data connectivity.
diagnostic_actions: node-network DNS/TCP probes for exact failing host
skill_outline: Identify which pull stage fails.
Probe the exact data endpoint from the affected network.
Repair the approved DNS link or egress rule and retry one pull.

discovery.gap: Most repair commands are networking/ACR commands outside the overlay.

held_out_variants: authentication failure rather than data failure

value_hypothesis.searches: Map a successful login plus failed blob download directly to the second endpoint.
value_hypothesis.actions: Avoid unrelated credential rotation and IAM work.

candidates.version_notes: Derive exact endpoint names and DNS resources from the registry/private-endpoint configuration; do not universalize a sample zone name.

candidates.task: Restore passwordless application access by repairing the broken identity layer.
candidates.prompt: Restore {workload}'s access to the approved resource using its existing workload identity. Preserve the image and resource settings, introduce no static credential, and verify access from the workload rather than your CLI session.
candidates.decision_boundary: Issuer/subject/audience mismatch breaks token exchange; a resource 403 after token success is a different authorization or network problem.
skill_outline: Classify token acquisition versus resource access failure.
Compare the exact identity tuple and actual pod configuration.
Repair one missing relationship and wait for propagation.
Verify the intended data-plane operation as that workload identity.

discovery.gap: Identity and SDK-centric paths may never enter AKS help.

success_oracle: correct workload principal succeeds at approved operation
held_out_variants: correct federation but missing data-plane role

value_hypothesis.searches: Replace repeated traversal of setup, federation and service RBAC docs.
value_hypothesis.actions: Avoid rebuilding the identity chain when only one link is wrong.

candidates.version_notes: Automatic preconfigures cluster-level OIDC/workload identity; pin the application SDK and distinguish direct federation from identity bindings.

candidates.task: Use an identity binding and direct federation in the same workload without breaking either.
candidates.prompt: The workload's identity-binding access works, but its direct federated identity fails with an audience mismatch. Restore both approved access paths without changing the existing binding's managed credential or broadening access.
candidates.decision_boundary: A projected token has one audience. api://AKSIdentityBinding cannot be reused as api://AzureADTokenExchange; bindings also require SDK opt-in and Kubernetes authorization.
skill_outline: Verify the cluster and SDK support identity bindings.
Keep the binding token/managed FIC unchanged.
Project a separate direct-federation token and route the correct client to its file.
Verify both identity flows and their resource permissions.
success_oracle: no audience overwrite breaking the first identity
negative_controls: use unsupported credential class or SDK

value_hypothesis.searches: Join recent AKS, Entra, SDK and token-projection facts in one recipe.

candidates.version_notes: Gate on current docs: identity bindings exclude API-server VNet integration. Do not assume Automatic supports the feature merely because workload identity is preconfigured. Pin SDK support and opt-in exactly.

candidates.task: Restore pending workloads by changing the correct NAP capacity constraint.
candidates.prompt: Restore the pending workloads using the existing approved pool configuration and capacity ceiling. Preserve workload requests, placement constraints and unrelated pools. Diagnose why capacity is not being provisioned before changing it.
candidates.decision_boundary: ARM agent pools and Karpenter NodePool CRDs are different. Dynamic NAP CPU/memory limits, static replicas/limits.nodes, Azure quota and pod constraints require different actions.
diagnostic_actions: regional quota only if evidence points there
skill_outline: Identify capacity owner and whether the pool is static or dynamic.
Distinguish no matching pool, exhausted pool limit, Azure quota and failed NodeClaim.
Change only the authorized constraint, then verify Ready nodes and scheduled workloads.

discovery.gap: A Kubernetes-only path may not encounter the overlay.

negative_controls: scale an ARM pool to fix a NAP CRD limit
raise Azure quota when only a NodePool limit is reached

value_hypothesis.searches: Resolve similarly named but distinct pool APIs and recent static-NAP semantics.
value_hypothesis.actions: Avoid irrelevant scaling updates and quota requests.

candidates.version_notes: Pin NAP CRD support. Static pools permit limits.nodes, not CPU/memory limits or weight; adding/removing replicas cannot switch an existing pool's mode.

candidates.task: Control image rollout timing without assuming the maintenance window governs all disruption.
candidates.prompt: Configure the approved weekly image maintenance window and diagnose why existing NAP nodes have not rolled to the new image. Preserve the workload disruption constraints and explain any remaining blocker with evidence.
candidates.decision_boundary: The AKS window controls when NAP picks up a new image; drift logic and node/pod disruption budgets control replacement. These decisions are separate from ordinary node-image channel assumptions.
skill_outline: Separate image availability/pickup from replacement eligibility.
Set the intended node OS schedule with reconciliation lead time.
Inspect the actual disruption blocker before changing budgets.
Verify new image state and preserved availability, or report a policy-backed block.
success_oracle: eligible nodes updated or precise blocked outcome
negative_controls: assume window closure cancels all in-flight work

value_hypothesis.searches: Combine maintenance and Karpenter disruption documentation.
value_hypothesis.actions: Avoid repeated channel/schedule updates that cannot remove the real blocker.

candidates.version_notes: Current NAP guide recommends at least 30 minutes lead time and four-hour windows. Model time explicitly rather than using wall-clock sleeps as the oracle.

candidates.task: Deploy within a fixed namespace budget when Automatic mutates resource defaults.
candidates.prompt: Restore the requested rollout within the existing namespace quota using the application's approved per-pod resources. Keep Automatic safeguards enforced, preserve placement requirements, and verify the admitted workload and Ready replicas.
candidates.decision_boundary: The effective admitted resource requests can differ from the submitted manifest. Missing resources may be defaulted; admission rejection, resource mutation and quota denial are different stages.
skill_outline: Compare submitted and effective resource fields before adding capacity.
Classify mutation versus denial and the named policy.
Set approved compliant resources/probes/image fields rather than disabling enforcement.
Verify effective admitted values, quota use and readiness.
success_oracle: requested replicas Ready within fixed quota

value_hypothesis.searches: Explain product-specific mutations and their interaction with quota in one procedure.
value_hypothesis.actions: Avoid wrong quota/scaling changes and repeated unchanged apply attempts.

candidates.version_notes: Pin policy version. Begin with unambiguous documented defaults; verify partial-resource mutation behavior against actual policy definitions before encoding it.

candidates.task: Resume an upgrade while preserving a workload availability floor.
candidates.prompt: Resume the failed pool upgrade while keeping the approved number of application replicas available. Temporary extra replicas are permitted within the stated capacity allowance; retain the PDB and restore the original replica count afterward.
candidates.decision_boundary: Eviction TooManyRequests due to zero disruptions is not an ARM throttle. Extra replicas help some budgets, but not every percentage/zero-unavailability policy.
skill_outline: Read the named blocker and budget math.
Create authorized healthy headroom and verify positive disruption allowance.
Retry the original scope/target and restore temporary replicas.
negative_controls: retry with no change in allowed disruptions

value_hypothesis.searches: Turn a named drain error into the correct availability-preserving branch.
value_hypothesis.actions: Avoid repeated failed upgrades and unrelated diagnostics.

candidates.version_notes: Requires a transition-history oracle, not the existing empty-PDB diagnostic fixture. Supported blocked outcomes must be distinct from successful repair.

candidates.task: Create a missing synced Kubernetes secret from an existing Key Vault object.
candidates.prompt: The application cannot find its expected Kubernetes secret even though the Key Vault object exists and access is configured. Repair CSI synchronization without copying secret material into manifests or broadening identity permissions. Verify consumption by the workload.
candidates.decision_boundary: secretObjects sync requires a live mounting pod, and objectName must match the mounted file/objectAlias rather than blindly copying the vault object name.
skill_outline: Confirm the correct namespace/reference and an actual consumer mount.
Compare object alias, mounted name and secretObjects mapping.
Repair the mapping or approved consumer, then verify sync and application use.

discovery.gap: The natural path may be entirely kubectl; verify help exposure before testing content efficacy.

negative_controls: reassign roles when mount already works
manual kubectl create secret from vault value
apply SecretProviderClass with no consumer and declare success

value_hypothesis.searches: Consolidate lifecycle and naming rules usually spread across setup/troubleshooting docs.
value_hypothesis.actions: Avoid redundant identity changes and repeated polling of a secret that cannot yet be synced.

candidates.version_notes: Use nonsecret version/hash sentinels for verification. Pin managed add-on behavior and CLI addon command availability.

candidates.task: Make an application observe a rotated secret through its actual consumption path.
candidates.prompt: The secret has rotated, but the application still reports the old configuration version. Restore use of the current version while preserving the approved rotation interval and identity settings. Do not expose secret contents.
candidates.decision_boundary: Mounted files/synced Secret objects can update, but process environment variables are captured at pod start; file consumers also need application reload behavior.
skill_outline: Locate the first stale layer: source, mount, synced object or application.
Use an authorized rolling restart for env consumers, or the application's supported reload path for file consumers.
Verify the application, not only the Secret object.

discovery.gap: A pure application/kubectl investigation may not see AKS help.

negative_controls: shorten polling when env is already stale
declare success from Secret metadata alone

value_hypothesis.searches: Resolve the consumption-mode distinction without broad secret-provider troubleshooting.
value_hypothesis.actions: Avoid waiting or reconfiguring a layer that is already current.

candidates.version_notes: Decide whether the goal is one-time recovery or ongoing automatic refresh; those require different oracles.

candidates.task: Recover new nodes that cannot obtain Overlay pod address space.
candidates.prompt: New nodes remain NotReady with pod-address allocation errors. Restore usable capacity within the approved address plan, preserving existing node/pod networking and avoiding cluster recreation.
candidates.decision_boundary: Overlay allocates per-node pod CIDR blocks; pod CIDR exhaustion differs from VNet subnet exhaustion or Azure VM quota. Expansion must meet platform and superset constraints.
skill_outline: Identify the exhausted address space.
Validate Linux IPv4 Overlay eligibility and a larger contiguous superset.
Apply the approved pod CIDR expansion and verify NNC plus node readiness.
negative_controls: declare success from ARM update only

value_hypothesis.searches: Join error-specific address allocation and expansion limitations.
value_hypothesis.actions: Avoid quota requests or disruptive recreation when an eligible expansion suffices.

candidates.version_notes: Pin published Linux/IPv4-only and contiguous-superset limitations; unsupported variants should produce a justified blocked outcome.

candidates.task: Restore the failing access path without weakening the working one.
candidates.prompt: kubectl can read resources, but logs and exec fail for the affected workload. Restore the failing operation while preserving the API endpoint exposure and authorized client ranges. Diagnose the failing stage before changing credentials or network rules.
candidates.decision_boundary: Client DNS/TCP, authentication, operation-specific authorization and API-server-to-kubelet connectivity are distinct. An unauthenticated 401 can demonstrate reachability.
diagnostic_actions: FQDN resolution and timed connectivity probe
skill_outline: Start from operations that already work.
Classify Forbidden versus timeout and client versus node path.
Repair only the authorized identity or network relationship.
Verify the failing operation and preservation of endpoint/range constraints.
success_oracle: no broad public exposure or admin-credential bypass
negative_controls: rotate credentials for a TCP timeout
open API ranges when only the node path fails
interpret expected unauthenticated 401 as network failure

value_hypothesis.searches: Compress a multi-guide connectivity decision tree into stage-specific diagnosis.

candidates.version_notes: Use customer-owned network controls in mutable fixtures; do not encode unsupported direct edits to AKS-managed node resources.

candidates.task: Publish an existing service through the appropriate managed Gateway API implementation.
candidates.prompt: Expose the existing HTTP service at the approved hostname using AKS application-routing Gateway API. Preserve the backend and existing working routes; verify an actual request before switching traffic.
candidates.decision_boundary: The app-routing GatewayClass is approuting-istio, not the mesh class istio. New Automatic 1.36+ defaults, older clusters, managed CRDs and incompatible mesh installations change the setup path.
skill_outline: Identify the installed implementation and managed prerequisites.
Reuse preconfigured Automatic features; enable only missing supported components.
Create the correct Gateway and route, verify status and real traffic, then cut over if requested.
success_oracle: old working path preserved until cutover
negative_controls: use mesh GatewayClass for app routing
treat resource creation as traffic success

value_hypothesis.searches: Resolve recent AKS-specific defaults and implementation naming without traversing multiple ingress guides.
value_hypothesis.actions: Avoid redundant feature installation and wrong-class resources.

candidates.version_notes: Pin the support matrix and CLI flags. Existing clusters do not automatically acquire every new-cluster default. Unsupported migration constraints require a separate blocked or migration-plan outcome.
